regret_risk: If the spike ships as written, the team keeps a priority-dev/ folder with its own Python project inside a plugin repository that is not an app, and 13 slices of one program in its tracker. The cost is a folder to move later. The gain is measured facts before the policy and the actuator exist.
summary: The design turns the open questions of priority.dev into 13 slices in 4 epics, ordered so that the cheapest probes of the largest unknowns come first. The three probes and the stop brief come before the log. Each unknown is a criterion in a blind rubric.
constraint_introduced: Code under priority-dev/ never imports from plugins/ or shared/, and the plugin tests never collect it. Only one module reads OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

findings.title: priority-dev/ has no bounded context yet
findings.detail: boundary_check reports priority-dev/ as uncovered. A canvas and a boundary record need code to verify against, so describe mode waits until slice 4 exists. Until then the constraint above is the only boundary.

findings.title: An application sits in a repository that is not an app
findings.detail: The plugin tests must not collect priority-dev/, and the install surface must not grow. A separate pyproject.toml inside priority-dev/ and a rule that no plugin imports it keep the two apart.

findings.title: Programs go through the tracker port
findings.detail: The program is seeded from goal.json and 04-slices.md with tracker.py, so no state is hand-edited. The beads data of this repository then holds priority-dev records. The engineer accepted this.

findings.title: The 0.90 gate fits a probe only through its rubric
findings.detail: A probe slice may refute its claim and still be correct. The blind rubric therefore scores the honesty and completeness of the report, not the size of the number.

findings.title: The model key must have one reader
findings.detail: The key lives in the environment and a single settings module reads it. The same rule as the stack card for a Python service holds: environment variables cross into code in one place only.
